title: BYD Bets on Hybrids to Crack India With Seal U and Atto 2
excerpt: The Chinese EV giant unveils its DM-i plug-in hybrid technology in India, confirming the Seal U SUV for a year-end launch and the compact Atto 2 as a follow-up.
body:
• BYD India has officially unveiled its DM-i plug-in hybrid technology, moving beyond its all-electric lineup for the first time
  • The Seal U PHEV SUV is confirmed for launch by end of 2026, priced around ₹45–50 lakh, with a claimed combined range of over 1,200 km
  • The compact Atto 2, spotted testing since August 2025, could follow at ₹18–25 lakh and directly challenge the Hyundai Creta EV and Maruti e-Vitara

BYD, the world's largest electric vehicle manufacturer, is making its most aggressive push yet into the Indian market — and this time, it's not going all-electric. The Chinese automaker has officially showcased its proprietary DM-i (Dual Mode Intelligent) plug-in hybrid technology in India, confirming two new models that will join its existing four-car EV lineup before the end of 2026.

The first to arrive will be the Seal U, a midsize PHEV SUV previously shown at Auto Expo 2025 under the Sealion 6 nameplate. The Atto 2, a compact SUV spotted testing on Indian roads since August 2025, is expected to follow shortly after.

Context

BYD currently sells four pure-electric models in India — the Atto 3, Seal sedan, eMAX 7 MPV, and Sealion 7 SUV. While the brand has built a global reputation on battery technology (its Blade Battery is used by other automakers, including Mahindra), India's EV adoption remains sluggish outside the two-wheeler segment. Charging infrastructure gaps, range anxiety, and steep sticker prices have kept four-wheeler EV penetration in single digits.

The DM-i technology is BYD's answer to that gap. Unlike conventional hybrids where the petrol engine does most of the work, DM-i follows an electric-first approach. The electric motor handles most driving situations while a 1.5-litre petrol engine acts primarily as a generator, kicking in only during high-speed cruising or heavy loads. BYD claims a thermal efficiency of 43.04 percent for the engine — among the highest in the industry — and a combined driving range of over 1,200 km on a full tank and charged battery.

"The introduction of DM-i technology marks a pivotal step in our commitment to making sustainable mobility more versatile and accessible for Indian consumers."

— Rajeev Chauhan, Head of Electric Passenger Vehicles, BYD India

Impact

The Seal U — a 4,775mm-long five-seater positioned against the Mahindra XEV 9e — will be BYD's first hybrid in India. Internationally sold in both front-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive configurations, it produces up to 323 hp and 550 Nm of torque, can sprint to 100 kph in 5.9 seconds, and offers up to 126 km of electric-only range. The India-spec model is expected to carry different specifications, but pricing is anticipated at ₹45–50 lakh, according to Autocar India.

The Atto 2 sits in a more competitive segment. At 4.3 metres long, the compact PHEV pairs the same 1.5-litre engine with either a 7.8 kWh or 18 kWh battery pack, delivering a combined range of up to 998 km and a pure electric range of roughly 39 km, according to DriveSpark. Estimated pricing of ₹18–25 lakh would put it squarely against upcoming electric SUVs from Hyundai, Maruti Suzuki, and Tata Motors — with the added insurance of a petrol backup.

BYD's hybrid pivot also reflects a broader strategic shift among Chinese automakers. In global markets where charging networks lag, PHEVs have been outselling pure EVs, and BYD's DM-i platform has already proven itself in China, where it powers several of the company's best-selling models. For India, a market where even wealthy urban buyers hesitate over apartment charging and highway infrastructure, the formula could prove more palatable than pure battery-electric.

What's Next

The Seal U is expected to launch by year-end 2026, making it BYD India's fifth model and its first with a combustion engine. Competition will come from JSW Motor's Jetour T2 PHEV, which is also expected to arrive by year-end at a similar price point. The Atto 2's timeline is less certain, though testing activity and its Autocar India listing suggest a 2026 launch remains possible.

For the Indian diaspora eyeing cars back home — whether for family or as an investment in the country's growing auto market — BYD's hybrid strategy signals that India is ready for a middle path between petrol and electric. The DM-i platform eliminates range anxiety while keeping running costs closer to an EV than a conventional car, a combination that could resonate with NRI buyers looking for practical, future-proof options for family members in India.

BYD's broader India ambitions remain significant. The company is reportedly investing in local assembly capacity, and a successful hybrid launch could lay the groundwork for a much larger product offensive — one that mirrors the playbook that made BYD the world's top-selling EV brand.
nri_angle: NRI buyers looking for practical, future-proof vehicle options for family in India get a middle-ground choice between petrol and electric with BYD's hybrid lineup.
